explain.say: Imagine New Year arriving on the very first day of spring, when flowers start to bloom. That is Nowruz, which means new day in Persian. Look at the checklist: it is how families get ready.

faq.a: Nowruz, meaning new day, is the Persian New Year, held at the spring equinox around 20 or 21 March. It is more than 3,000 years old and celebrated by people of many faiths.

faq.q: What is on a Haft-sin table?
faq.a: Seven items whose Persian names begin with S, such as sabzeh sprouts, samanu pudding, senjed dried fruit, seer garlic, seeb apples, somagh sumac and serkeh vinegar. Many families add a mirror, candles and goldfish.
More than 300 million people, in Iran, Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Kurdish communities, Central Asia, parts of India and Pakistan, and families around the world.
On the 13th day of Nowruz, families spend the day outdoors with a picnic. Many throw their sabzeh sprouts into running water for good luck.
asks: What happens on the 13th day of Nowruz?

faq.q: Why is Nowruz on the first day of spring?
faq.a: It begins at the spring equinox, when day and night are about equal and nature wakes up again, a natural start for a new year.

facts: Nowruz begins at the spring equinox, around 20 or 21 March.
Nowruz is on UNESCO's list of Intangible Cultural Heritage, and the UN marks 21 March as International Nowruz Day.

wrong.1: The special table is called the Haft-sin.
